root_idea.summary: The root centers on following, coming after, pursuing, or tracing something or someone.
root_idea.development: The basic orientation is physical following or pursuit; related formations distinguish catching up or causing something to follow, adherence to a path or instruction, succession, followers, and claims pursued against another.

senses.definition: To follow, go behind or after, pursue, or overtake someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for physical following or pursuit and for coming after another; the precise result may range from trailing behind to catching up.

senses.definition: To follow a person, model, path, teaching, or command in conduct; to imitate or act according to it.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of physical following, including adherence to guidance and acting in accordance with what another has done or prescribed.

senses.definition: To follow after, pursue, or catch up with someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used where the subject comes after or reaches what has gone before; passive forms describe being followed or pursued.

senses.definition: To make someone or something follow, overtake, or come after another; to cause one thing to follow another.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative construction may take a person or thing as the one made to follow, and may express successive placement or pursuit.

senses.definition: To follow, pursue, or go after a person, thing, course, or report.
senses.usage_conditions: The following may be physical or figurative; the form is also used for pursuing desires, conjectures, or a chosen course.

senses.definition: To adhere to, obey, or follow a person, guidance, teaching, path, or instruction.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which following means adopting a direction, belief, example, or command and acting in accordance with it.

senses.definition: Following one another consecutively; successive and uninterrupted.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic dual expression, two items occur in immediate succession.

senses.definition: Followed by others; one whom others pursue or follow.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a person or thing that is the object of following or pursuit.

senses.definition: A follower; one who comes after or follows another.
senses.usage_conditions: May describe a person or thing following in another's track and may function as a collective or quasi-plural expression.
In the Quranic construction concerning those without sexual interest, the word is explained as an attendant of the household.
A collective or quasi-plural noun denoting people who are subordinate followers of someone else.

senses.definition: A claimant or avenger who pursues a right, blood-revenge, or redress against another.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, the word can denote one who prosecutes or sues for what has been denied or withheld.

senses.definition: An aider or supporter against an enemy.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative interpretation of the Quranic expression, emphasizing one who can pursue or assist against an adversary.

senses.definition: Following or pursuing a person, thing, course, or opinion.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of following, including adherence to a view or reliance on conjecture.

senses.definition: Pursuing a claim for bloodwit after remission, with fair conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: In the construction اتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ, it denotes orderly prosecution or follow-up of the bloodwit claim rather than retaliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To refer a creditor to another person for payment, or accept such a transfer to a solvent debtor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A financial and legal construction used with the relevant prepositions for referral of a debt.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause one thing to follow another, whether for good or evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II causative expression concerning the succession of an event or thing after another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Consecution or succession: making two actions, affairs, or performances follow one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of consecutive performance, uninterrupted continuation, or carrying an activity forward in sequence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uniformly trimming or paring a bow, part after part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical description of executing each successive portion evenly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an action, work, or speech sound, complete, and free from defect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form III use applied to work, language, or performance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For pasture to fatten and improve cattle thoroughly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use with pasture as the subject and camels or cattle as the affected animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, assist, or help someone in carrying out an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form III construction with a person as the one assisted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pursue, investigate, examine, or search for something repeatedly and step by step.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The search may proceed successively, gradually, or by following traces and details.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become consecutive, successive, or uninterrupted; for people or things to follow one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of events, rains, years, people, or objects occurring in succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a horse to run evenly and continuously without uneven lifting of its limbs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a horse's regular movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For camels to become fat and goodly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use concerning the condition of camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To desire, demand, or cause someone to follow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X construction may express a request for following or the resulting causation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A follower or persistent pursuer, especially a passionate lover or sedulous seeker of women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use describing persistent attachment or pursuit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose speech proceeds consecutively, one part following another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of connected and orderly discourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cow that desires and follows the bull.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized feminine animal adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The consequence or result of an action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used of an adverse or consequential result for which someone may be held responsible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A claim or due pursued because of injury, wrongdoing, or property-related liability.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The claim may be a right attached to property or a demand for redress against the person responsible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A debtor who is prosecuted or sued for property or a right owed to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is passive in force: the person is one pursued by a creditor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young cow or calf in its first year, named because it follows its mother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also associated with the animal's early age; later juristic explanations about its horns and ears are not the lexical basis of the word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A title for the kings of Yemen who ruled Himyar and Hadramawt; by extension, a particular king of that line.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained through the succession of rulers; it is also used in Quranic discussion of the people or king of Tubbaʿ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chief or largest bee, whom the other bees follow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized collective-animal term, with a plural referring to such leaders.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of flying creature or bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source gives the term as a bird name without further zoological specification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The shade or shadow that follows the sun or a person; in one interpretation, the asterism Aldebaran.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The poetic interpretation is disputed: some authorities understand shade, while another explanation identifies Aldebaran.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disliked wind that begins near sunrise, veers through the directions, and returns to its starting direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical name for a recurring early-morning wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The legs of a beast, understood as parts that follow one another in sequence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized or epithet-like use applied specifically to an animal's legs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A male genie that accompanies and follows a woman; تَابِعَةٌ is the corresponding female genie associated with a man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A folkloric usage also extended to female associates or attendants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A member of the generation following the Companions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical religious-historical designation based on chronological succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The follower of the Pleiades, namely Aldebaran or the Hyades asterism.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the star's following position relative to the Pleiades; variant identifications are reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The rhetorical addition of an imitative or echoing word after another for emphasis, fullness, or corroboration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The second word may be meaningless on its own or may retain an independent meaning; the construction includes expressions such as حَسَنٌ بَسَنٌ and هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Assimilation of one word or vowel to another in form or pronunciation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical grammatical and phonological extension of the rhetorical notion of making one element follow another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female animal or servant that has offspring following her.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a ewe, she-goat, cow, or female servant accompanied by its or her young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything made or executed soundly, thoroughly, and free from defect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial use describing a completed or well-executed result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Even, uniform, or consistently ordered in its parts; symmetrical or internally consistent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied figuratively to a branch without knots, a well-proportioned horse, or consistent knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing that follows another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A generic nominal use for what comes after or follows something else.
